# Sign change of the square-hexagonal difference of the three-body lattice energy $T_\nu$ at $\nu_c\approx 3.92$ in two dimensions

## Abstract

We study the three-body energy $T_\nu(L)$ of two-dimensional Bravais lattices $L$ of unit covolume, a sum of $(|x||y||x-y|)^{-\nu}$ over ordered pairs of distinct nonzero lattice vectors [C-modell]. The question is whether $f(\nu)=T_\nu(\text{square})-T_\nu(\text{hexagonal})$ changes sign, which would signal a hexagonal-to-square transition, and whether the sign change lies in an interval of width at most 0.05 [C-lattice-R1]. A targeted search of 45 abstracts did not find this statement in the literature [C-lattice-R1]. Numerically, $f(3.9)=$ `5.300e-03` and $f(3.94)=$ `-6.238e-03`, so $f$ changes sign between $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$ [C-lattice-R1]. The energies are computed by cube summation with Richardson extrapolation in the cutoff [C-modell]. The main limitation is that the result is a numerical observation with an error estimate. It carries no rigorous certificate, and the location of $\nu_c$ inside the interval is not established.

## Introduction

The three-body energy $T_\nu$ assigns to each Bravais lattice of unit covolume a sum over triangles with a vertex at the origin [C-modell]. For two-dimensional lattices, a natural question is which lattice minimizes $T_\nu$ and how this depends on the exponent $\nu$. The square and hexagonal lattices are the two obvious candidates. If the preferred lattice among them switches as $\nu$ varies, there is a critical exponent $\nu_c$ at which $f(\nu)=T_\nu(\text{square})-T_\nu(\text{hexagonal})$ vanishes.

No literature claim is available to us here. In a targeted search of 45 abstracts on 2026-10-04 we did not find the statement below [C-lattice-R1]. This is a statement about the search only and not a claim of priority.

We report a numerical observation that $f$ changes sign between $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$ [C-lattice-R1]. This places a critical exponent in an interval of width at most 0.05 [C-lattice-R1]. The evidence is two evaluations with an error estimate. We do not prove the sign change.

**Summary of results.**

- Observation 1 shows that $f$ is positive at $\nu=3.9$ and negative at $\nu=3.94$, so $f$ changes sign between these two exponents [C-lattice-R1].
- Together with continuity of $f$ in $\nu$, assumed and not proved here, this localizes $\nu_c$ to an interval of width at most 0.05 (Observation 1) [C-lattice-R1].
- All results are numerical and carry no rigorous certificate (Method, Discussion).

## Model and assumptions

Let $P(L)$ be the set of ordered pairs $(x,y)$ of distinct nonzero vectors of a two-dimensional Bravais lattice $L$. We define
$$T_\nu(L)=\sum_{(x,y)\in P(L)}\frac{1}{(|x|\,|y|\,|x-y|)^{\nu}} .$$
Lattices are normalized to covolume $1$ [C-modell]. A lattice is parametrized by $\tau=x+iy$ in the fundamental domain. The square lattice and the hexagonal lattice are the two points of this domain compared below. We write
$$f(\nu)=T_\nu(\text{square})-T_\nu(\text{hexagonal}).$$

Fixed model parameters [C-modell]:

- covolume $=1$ for all Bravais lattices [C-modell];
- cutoff $R \in \{32, 48, 64, 96\}$, with the summation cube $[-R, R]^d$ in lattice coordinates and Richardson extrapolation in $R$ [C-modell];
- $\nu_{\mathrm{direct}}=12$: for $\nu \ge 12$, direct summation replaces FFT convolution [C-modell].

Assumption (A): $f$ is continuous in $\nu$ on the interval considered. It is used only to pass from a sign change of two sampled values to a zero. It is not checked here.

## Method

The sign change is established numerically. The two values of $f$ are obtained from cube summation, combined by Richardson extrapolation in $R$, and accompanied by an error estimate [C-modell, C-lattice-R1]. The sign of $f$ at each of the two sample points is then compared with the size of the error estimate.

We separate three classes of statements.

- *Proved statements:* none.
- *Computer-assisted rigorous statements:* none. No exact rational arithmetic, symbolic positivity proof or interval enclosure underlies the main observation.
- *Numerical observations:* the sign of $f$ at $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$, and the resulting sign-change interval [C-lattice-R1].

The trusted base is the floating-point summation code and the extrapolation in $R$. A third party can re-run the computation with the commands in the Declarations. Anything beyond the two stated values, in particular the precise location of $\nu_c$, counts at most as a numerical candidate.

## Results

::: observation [Sign change of $f$ between $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$]
In two dimensions, the difference $f(\nu)=T_\nu(\text{square})-T_\nu(\text{hexagonal})$ changes sign between $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$ (numerically, with error estimate) [C-lattice-R1]. The verifier values are $f(3.9)=$ `5.300e-03` and $f(3.94)=$ `-6.238e-03` [C-lattice-R1]. Under Assumption (A), a zero of $f$, that is a critical exponent $\nu_c$, lies in an interval of width at most 0.05 [C-lattice-R1].
:::

*Certificate.* The verifier recomputed $f$ at the two sample points with the model parameters of the Model section. It checked the sign at each point against the error estimate [C-lattice-R1, C-modell]. No exact or interval certificate is available. The existence of a zero between the sample points rests on Assumption (A).

Novelty status: not found in a targeted search of 45 abstracts on 2026-10-04 [C-lattice-R1].

This article records no negative result of its own. Adversarial counter-checks of the main observation are reported in Appendix A.

## Discussion, limitations and open questions

The observation shows that $T_\nu(\text{square})-T_\nu(\text{hexagonal})$ is positive at $\nu=3.9$ and negative at $\nu=3.94$ [C-lattice-R1]. It does not show which lattice is the global minimizer at other exponents. Only the two lattices in the difference were compared. The sign change is numerical, and the zero between the sample points is inferred under Assumption (A).

- (i) Can the location of the sign change between $\nu=3.9$ and $\nu=3.94$ be narrowed by evaluating $f$ at further exponents [C-lattice-R1]?
- (ii) Can the sign of $f$ at the two sample points be certified with interval arithmetic, so that the sign change becomes computer-assisted rigorous?
- (iii) Which lattice minimizes $T_\nu$ over the whole fundamental domain on either side of the sign change?
